written: 2026-11-13, committed before any Actions probe of this follow-up ran: why the harness case 'A0's controller on its target's orientation' took 31.1 s on the release push at b1de6f7c (run 43345746689, 3.12 shard 16), and whether #283 made it, and the first payer of the scan's build, slower
labels: predictions by the author from the junit files of the push run and of the four probe runs of #283 (read, not re-run); the Actions arms are the measurement
seen_before: run 43345746689 (b1de6f7c), shard 16: the case took 31.1 s on Python 3.12, 6.0 s on 3.13 and 3.7 s on 3.14; its two siblings took 5.2 and 1.2 s on 3.12; the three cases share a compiled A0 controller, so the first of them to run on a worker pays it

the probes of #283 at the base (da8d1679), shard 16: the case took 5.2 to 9.7 s in 5 arms, and a sibling ('A0's controller, the body's z along the home pose's x') took 49.3 and 71.9 s in 2 arms: the payer is whichever case a worker reaches first

the same probes' junit: test_every_guard (the scan's first payer in shard 16): wall 265 to 404 s and CPU 284 to 428 s at the base, wall 418 to 700 s and CPU 362 to 641 s at the head, jax_compile_s 118 to 157 s at the base and 196 to 384 s at the head; the head's arms with jax.clear_caches switched off: 526 and 700 s wall, compile 235 and 308 s

operating_point.platform: GitHub runner, 4 vCPU, Python 3.12, CPU; 'alone' arms pinned to one CPU with taskset
operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: as CI runs shard 16: pytest -m 'not slow' -n auto --dist worksteal --mime-shard 16/30; base is da8d1679 (src and tests checked out over the probe branch), head is b1de6f7c
operating_point.seeds_and_draws: alone arms: 3 interleaved pairs for the A0 cases, 2 for the scan's first payer; in-shard arms: 4 of each

gate_1_a0_case_alone.claim: the three A0 cases of the harness, run alone in one process on one CPU, cost the same at da8d1679 and b1de6f7c, and the first of them takes over 30 s
gate_1_a0_case_alone.case: tests/saved/test_switch_harness.py::test_replacing_every_fallback_changes_nothing_where_its_condition_is_false with -k "A0's controller", the three cases in file order

prediction.why: 37.4 s alone on the push run's re-run; the sibling at the base took 49 and 72 s in-shard

gate_1_a0_case_alone.metric: the first case's time, and the three cases' sum, base against head

control.plant: none: the base arm of the same pair is the control
control.expected_rate: head within 15 % of base in 3 of 3 pairs

gate_1_a0_case_alone.if_wrong: head slower than base by over 15 % in the pairs: #283 cost the case, and the next arm (compiled programs dropped) says how
gate_1_a0_case_alone.cannot_discriminate_if: the first case is under 10 s alone (the compile was cached on the runner), or the pairs differ by more among themselves than head from base

gate_2_cache_clear_cost.claim: building the scan's traced steps first in the process (which empties JAX's caches once) does not slow the A0 cases that run after it on the same worker
gate_2_cache_clear_cost.case: head only: the same three cases in a process that first calls switch_configurations.traced_steps() in collection_finish (not timed), on one CPU, against the head's cases alone

prediction.why: the emptying happens once, before the first trace, at the start of the worker's life; nothing the A0 cases need has been compiled by then, and the traces the build makes compile nothing

control.plant: none; the arm is a comparison

gate_2_cache_clear_cost.if_wrong: slower after the build: the emptying (or the build's own churn) costs later tests, and the fix is to restore or avoid it
gate_2_cache_clear_cost.cannot_discriminate_if: the case is under 10 s in both

gate_3_first_payer_alone.claim: the scan's first payer in shard 16 (test_every_guard_...) alone on one CPU takes the same at the base and the head

prediction.why: the emptied caches change no work the test needs (the scan build was 206 s with and without it locally); the in-shard 1.5 to 1.7 times is then contention (XLA's compile threads spin, so CPU seconds inflate with the wall time), not code

gate_3_first_payer_alone.if_wrong: slower alone at the head: the cause is in the code of #283 and not in the shard's schedule
gate_3_first_payer_alone.cannot_discriminate_if: the two base runs differ by over 15 % between themselves

gate_4_in_shard.claim: in shard 16 as CI runs it, the sum of the three A0 cases and the first payer's time and CPU seconds, base against head

prediction.value: the A0 sum is the same distribution at both (one case pays, 5 to 70 s); the first payer is 1.4 to 1.8 times slower at the head, as in #283's probes

gate_4_in_shard.if_wrong: the A0 sum differs: the schedule changes who compiles what
gate_4_in_shard.cannot_discriminate_if: the arms' CPU models differ between base and head: they are paired by the CPU model in the report

bits._how: no program changes: a test-suite allowlist row and, if a measurement asks for it, test infrastructure

outcomes._note: written after the probes; the predictions above are unchanged. Runs 43349096705, 43351872173, 43354131525 on probe/scan-followup (deleted).
outcomes.gate_1_a0_case_alone: as predicted: the first of the three cases alone on one CPU took 57.5, 57.1, 56.9 s at da8d1679 and 57.0, 57.3, 57.2 s at b1de6f7c (Xeon 8370C), 43.6, 42.9, 42.9 and 43.1, 42.9, 43.4 s (EPYC 9V74); over 30 s at both, equal within 1 %. The band 28 to 60 s held. The first run of this arm (43349096705) selected nothing (-k with a space is a syntax error in pytest) and measured nothing.
outcomes.gate_2_cache_clear_cost: as predicted, and then some: with the scan's traced steps built first in the process the first case took 25.4 and 19.7 s, less than the 57.0 and 43.1 s without (the build warms what the case compiles); no slowdown from the emptied caches.
outcomes.gate_3_first_payer_alone: as predicted: test_every_guard alone on one CPU 352.5 s (base) and 351.2 s (head) on EPYC 7763, 261.2 and 259.0 s on EPYC 9V45. The shard's 1.5 to 1.7 times is not in the code.
outcomes.gate_4_in_shard: partly: the first payer took 255 to 367 s at the base (4 arms) and 602 to 700 s at the head (4 arms), as before; the A0 cases: one paid at the base in one arm (86.7 s, a sibling), none over 11 s at the head in 8 arms. Unpredicted and measured: the head with xdist's own scheduler (pinning off) took 500 to 738 s (4 arms), and the BASE with only the first payer marked fixture_first (so stock xdist sorts it to the head of the collection) took 595 to 731 s (3 arms): the early start, concurrent with the other workers' first compiles, is what makes it slower in the shard, not the pinning, the emptied caches (arms with the clearing off: 526 and 700 s) or the scan's tracing. The mechanism of the slowdown (contention for the 4 vCPUs) is a hypothesis.
